title: Separated locally quasi-finite geometry of an affine etale relation
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $U$ be an affine $S$-scheme, meaning a scheme isomorphic to $\operatorname{Spec}A$ for a commutative ring $A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $R$ be an $S$-scheme and let $j=(s,t):R\to U\times_SU$ [def-pc-fibre-product] be a monomorphism such that $R(T)$ is an equivalence relation on $U(T)$ for every $S$-scheme $T$. Suppose $s,t:R\to U$ are etale [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Then each of the three morphisms $s$, $t$, and $j$ is separated [def-weil-proper-morphism] and locally quasi-finite [pqf-def-quasifinite]. No separatedness hypothesis on $S$ and no quasi-compactness hypothesis on $R$ are imposed.

source.place: Tag 0265, lemma-presentation-quasi-compact, first two paragraphs of the proof (separatedness of R, s, t and j, and local quasi-finiteness of j); local quasi-finiteness of s,t is the unramified consequence used in the first representability step.

proof.text: Write $V=U\times_SU$ and $P=U\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}U$. If $U\cong\operatorname{Spec}A$, the affine fibre-product formula gives $P\cong\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_{\mathbf Z}A)$, so $P$ is affine. Let $k:V\to P$ be the morphism with the same two projections to $U$ as $V$. It is a monomorphism: for any two morphisms $a,b:T\to V$, equality $ka=kb$ gives equality of both projections of $a,b$ to $U$, and hence $a=b$ by the defining universal property of $V$. Therefore $q=k\circ j:R\to P$ is a monomorphism too: $qa=qb$ first implies $ja=jb$ by cancellation of $k$, and then $a=b$ by cancellation of $j$.

source.place: Tag 0265, lemma-presentation-quasi-compact, first proof paragraph; affine product formula: Schemes Tag 01I4, lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes

proof.text: For $f=j:R\to V$ and for $f=q:R\to P$, write $p_1,p_2:R\times_{\operatorname{target}(f)}R\to R$. Since $f$ is a monomorphism, $fp_1=fp_2$ implies $p_1=p_2$. The diagonal $\Delta_f$ is inverse to $p_1$: $p_1\Delta_f=1_R$, and both projections of $\Delta_fp_1$ agree with those of the identity, so $\Delta_fp_1=1$ by the fibre-product universal property. Thus both diagonals are isomorphisms. An isomorphism identifies the source with the whole target, a closed and open subset, and induces isomorphisms on structure sheaves; by the definitions it is both a closed and an open immersion. Consequently $j,q$ are separated and $\Delta_j$ is an open immersion. This proves the elementary monomorphism-diagonal argument of Schemes Tags 01L3 and 01L4 explicitly.

source.place: Tags 01L3, lemma-monomorphism, and 01L4, lemma-monomorphism-separated; applied in the first paragraph of the proof of Spaces Tag 0265

proof.text: Apply the separated-over-affine lemma to $q:R\to P$: step 1 gives that $P$ is affine, and step 2 gives that $q$ is separated. It follows that the absolute structure morphism $a_R:R\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is separated. Write $a_U:U\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ for the absolute structure morphism. Since $a_U\circ s=a_R=a_U\circ t$, separated cancellation, clause (b), applied to these two factorizations shows that $s$ and $t$ are separated. Together with step 2 this gives separatedness of all three requested morphisms. The argument uses the affine scheme $P$, and makes no assumption on the diagonal of $S$.

source.place: Tag 0265, lemma-presentation-quasi-compact, first proof paragraph; Schemes Tag 01KV, lemma-compose-after-separated

proof.text: By the definition of etale, each of $s,t$ is unramified. Apply the unramified-to-locally-quasi-finite theorem to each morphism to obtain that $s,t$ are locally quasi-finite, in the pointwise sense of the statement. The definition of unramified also gives that $s$ is locally of finite type. This deduction requires no quasi-compactness or separatedness hypothesis on an unramified morphism.

source.place: Tag 0265, lemma-presentation-quasi-compact, first representability step, citing Morphisms Tag 02V5, lemma-unramified-quasi-finite; Morphisms Tag 02GV, lemma-flat-unramified-etale

proof.text: Let $\pi_1:V\to U$ be the first projection. The equality $\pi_1\circ j=s$ and the local finite type of $s$ from step 4 allow clause (f) of the permanence lemma to be applied to $j$ followed by $\pi_1$; it yields that $j$ is locally of finite type. Step 2 already gives that $\Delta_j$ is an open immersion. These are exactly the two conditions in the definition of an unramified morphism, so $j$ is unramified. Apply the unramified-to-locally-quasi-finite theorem once more to get that $j$ is locally quasi-finite. This supplies the local quasi-finiteness required in the second paragraph of the source, using its monomorphism hypothesis through the explicitly computed diagonal. Combining steps 2--5 proves every clause. Nothing in these steps assumes quasi-compactness of $R$.

lean.statement: theorem affine_etale_relation_separated_locally_quasi_finite {S : Scheme.{u}} (R U : Over S) [IsAffine U.left] (s t : R ⟶ U) [Mono (pullback.lift s.left t.left (s.w.trans t.w.symm))] (hrel : ∀ T : Over S, Equivalence (fun a b : T ⟶ U ↦ ∃ r : T ⟶ R, r ≫ s = a ∧ r ≫ t = b)) [Etale s.left] [Etale t.left] : (IsSeparated s.left ∧ Scheme.Hom.IsLocallyQuasiFinite s.left) ∧ (IsSeparated t.left ∧ Scheme.Hom.IsLocallyQuasiFinite t.left) ∧ (IsSeparated (pullback.lift s.left t.left (s.w.trans t.w.symm)) ∧ Scheme.Hom.IsLocallyQuasiFinite (pullback.lift s.left t.left (s.w.trans t.w.symm)))
